text:
alex: quick heads-up — after yesterday's runtime deploy i'm seeing a ~4–9ms p50 bump on short (<=16) sequences. flame points at host-side tokenization + small-write fragmentation over gRPC. anyone else?

maya: yep, saw p99 spikes on the canary too. repro locally with `make bench-mini`.

otto: grabbed an strace/proc trace. lots of `writev(2)` syscalls with 100-300B payloads, not being coalesced. looks like ingress proxy is flushing per-chunk.

sam: interesting — kernel selection probably fine. this smells like our streaming chunker/flush policy. perf snapshot from a request: 

```
# simplified trace (host-side)
tokenize           0.6ms
preparse.shim      1.8ms  <-- many small copies
writev x12         2.4ms  <-- 12 small syscalls, avg 220B
tls_write          1.0ms
total host-overhead 5.8ms
```

maya: trace also shows KV cache hits are frequent but cheap; the copy churn in preparse seems larger than expected.

alex: i ran an A/B: disable streaming-chunking on the gateway for short responses -> p50 returns to baseline. so chunking heuristics + small writes are the trigger.

perf-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary rollback at 3123458000.

otto: quick list of mitigations i see: 1) coalesce small chunks in ingress proxy write buffer (batch short writes for <1ms), 2) change low-latency batch hint to avoid per-token flush, 3) try `TCP_CORK` / `SO_SNDBUF` tweaks on warmup, 4) reduce copies in preparse by passing iovec straight through.

sam: i'll prototype a minimal coalescer in the proxy (ring buffer + timer) today. i think easiest win.

maya: i'll add telemetry counters: `writev_count`, `avg_writev_size`, `preparse_copy_bytes` and wire p50/p99 for them into the console. helps correlate.

alex: otto please run microbench varying write sizes (64/128/256/512/1k) and include kernel-mode vs user-mode coalescing. post results here.

otto: will do. also double-check grpc core socket options; we've seen earlier versions flush aggressively.

sam: note re: kvcache — if we change copy strategy, ensure KV value pinning doesn't extend latency tail via memcopy. i'll watch mempressure.

maya: filed a short ticket with repro steps and perf artifacts: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENGRT-1432 (notes + flame + trace)

alex: plan of record: rollback canary, sam PR for coalesce, maya telemetry, otto microbench, then re-canary with coalescer on. aim to re-evaluate in 24h. :thumbsup:

sam: ack, starting prototype.

otto: ack, benching now.

maya: ack, instrumenting.

alex: thanks all — keep updates short in this thread.
